glosses: dative plural of Abklatsch
gerund of abklatschen
to rebound, bounce off with a clapping sound
to fend off, return something (such as a ball) by hitting it with a clapping sound
to high five someone or give them a pat on the back (in the literal sense); to exchange high-fives with someone

examples.text: Ab Freitag früh um 8 Uhr haben sie wieder getobt und sind über den Rasen gehüpft, die sonst so zurückhaltenden Golfprofis, sie haben die Fans angestachelt, gebrüllt, sich enthusiastisch abgeklatscht.
examples.translation: Early on Friday by 8 o'clock they were in a frenzy again and hopping over the turf, those otherwise so reserved golf pros, they were exciting the fans, screaming, enthusiastically high-fiving each other.
examples.english: Early on Friday by 8 o'clock they were in a frenzy again and hopping over the turf, those otherwise so reserved golf pros, they were exciting the fans, screaming, enthusiastically high-fiving each other.

glosses: to give (someone) a pat to indicate something (to them), e.g. to cut in on a dance or to tag someone in a game of tag
to applaud or acclaim someone or something
to obtain an encore from someone by clapping

examples.text: Die Zuschauer haben dem Magier noch einen Zaubertrick abgeklatscht.
examples.translation: The spectators encored another magic trick from the magician.
examples.english: The spectators encored another magic trick from the magician.

glosses: to break off a rehearsal, etc. by clapping
to lightly, repeatedly strike or clap someone ((+ mit) with something), making a clapping sound
to decisively defeat someone (especially in sports)
to produce a mirror image impression copy of
to quickly print from forms, off of the press
to copycat, to produce a poor imitation of
to portray something incompletely; to sketch, outline
